newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka seeks to increase trade with Italy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka seeks to increase trade with Italy.

text.p: Sri Lanka, seeking investments from Italy, has invited Italian businessmen to visit Colombo to attend a major trade fair in November to scout for joint ventures, a foreign ministry statement said on Thursday.

The statement said that Sri Lankan Minister for Trade and Commerce Kingsley Wickremaratne had inaugurated the Italy-Sri Lanka Joint Business Council, aimed at increasing business ties between the two countries, during a recent visit to Rome.
The minister told Italian businessmen that they could use the fair to scout for joint ventures and sub-contracting for component manufacture.

Bilateral trade between the two countries in 1995 was in favour of Sri Lanka. Sri Lankan exports to Italy, mostly garments and ceramic products, were worth 3.7 billion rupees and imports from Italy, mostly electrical goods, leather products and chemicals, were worth 3.25 billion rupees, a commerce ministry official said.
Figures for 1996 were not immediately available.
